title: Pansy bookmark in petit point
subtitle: A narrow bookmark with a single pansy worked in tent stitch on 18-count canvas
excerpt: A small bookmark worked in tent stitch on 18-count canvas, with a single pansy in five shades at the centre and a plain single-colour border. Petit point on this fine canvas gives precise petal shading in a narrow strip format.
sourceNotes: Pansy motif adapted from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), petit point and canvaswork flower chapter. Weldon's Practical Needlework, petit point series.

glossaryTerms.definition: Needlepoint worked on a fine canvas of 18 count or higher, using tent stitch. The smaller stitch scale allows more detailed shading and finer outlines than standard 13-count work.

heroPrompt: A slender needlepoint bookmark in purple and yellow pansy motif on cream, resting in an open hardback book, close-up showing the fine stitch detail, natural light.

content.text: This bookmark uses
petit point

tent stitch on 18-count canvas to work a single pansy with detailed petal shading. The strip is 22 holes wide by 126 holes tall, finishing at 3 cm wide by 18 cm long. Stranded cotton gives a smoother, slightly shinier finish than wool on fine canvas.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 18-count mono canvas, cut 8 by 24 cm (leaves a 2.5 cm margin around the 22 by 126 hole design area)

items.label: Thread: petal dark
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC 333 / Anchor 119 (very dark blue violet). About 1.5 m

items.label: Thread: petal medium
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC 340 / Anchor 118 (medium blue violet). About 1.5 m

items.label: Thread: petal light
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC 341 / Anchor 117 (light blue violet). About 1.5 m

items.label: Thread: petal centre
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC 726 / Anchor 295 (light topaz). About 0.5 m

items.label: Thread: petal centre dark
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC 310 / Anchor 403 (black). About 0.5 m

items.label: Thread: background
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC 746 / Anchor 275 (off white). About 4 m

items.label: Backing ribbon
items.value: Narrow grosgrain ribbon, 2 cm wide by 20 cm long

content.text: Palette
Petal dark: DMC 333 / Anchor 119: very dark blue violet
Petal medium: DMC 340 / Anchor 118: medium blue violet
Petal light: DMC 341 / Anchor 117: light blue violet
Petal centre: DMC 726 / Anchor 295: light topaz
Petal centre dark: DMC 310 / Anchor 403: black
Background: DMC 746 / Anchor 275: off white
Stretching the canvas
Fine canvas can be worked in the hand for a narrow strip. Roll the unworked section loosely as you work down the length. A hoop is optional but helps keep the canvas taut for the detailed petal area.
Stitches used
Continental tent stitch
throughout. Use 2 strands of stranded cotton on 18-count canvas.
Working method
Locate the centre of the strip (hole 63 of the 126-hole length). The pansy is centred on holes 40 to 80.

Work the five pansy petals. The two upper petals use the darkest shade for the lower half and the medium shade for the upper half. The three lower petals use the medium shade with light shading at the tips.
Work the yellow centre circle in the topaz shade. Add four or five black stitches at the inner edge of the centre to represent the radiating lines.
Fill the off-white background across the rest of the strip.
Press the finished strip lightly between two damp cloths rather than full blocking, to preserve the fine texture of the petit point.
Finishing
Trim the canvas margin to 1 cm. Fold to the back. Slip-stitch the narrow ribbon to the back to cover the margins and neaten the edges. Fold the short ends under and slip-stitch them closed.
What to try next

A small square petit point panel in a frame uses the same 18-count canvas and the same stranded cotton but allows more complex shading across a larger motif. Victorian miniature portrait reproductions used this scale.
